S2D4P.generic.aggregator module

class S2D4P.generic.aggregator.MetricsAggregator(distributed: Distributed, name: str, epoch_metric_terms: dict[str, list[float]] | None = None, epoch_times: list[float] | None = None, num_epochs_seen: int = 0)

Bases: object

Accumulate and aggregate training or validation metrics.

Batch-level losses, learning rates, and auxiliary scalar values are summed locally and can be reduced across distributed processes. Aggregated epoch metrics and elapsed times are retained for checkpointing and plotting.

Parameters:

  • distributed (Distributed) – Distributed runtime used to reduce metrics across processes.

  • name (str) – Name identifying the metric collection, such as training or validation.

  • epoch_metric_terms (dict[str, list[float]] | None) – Previously recorded epoch-level metrics keyed by metric name.

  • epoch_times (list[float] | None) – Previously recorded elapsed times for each epoch.

  • num_epochs_seen (int) – Number of epochs represented by the stored history.

epoch_times: list[float] | None = None

Restore stored epoch metric state.

Parameters:

state_dict (dict) – Saved aggregator state containing metric histories, timing information, and epoch counts.

name: str
num_epochs_seen: int = 0
classmethod plot(aggregator_list: list[MetricsAggregator], color_styles_list: list[tuple[str, str]] = None, plot_dir: str | Path | None = None, figsize=(8, 5)) → None

Plot and save recorded epoch metrics.

A separate plot and CSV file are generated for each recorded metric. Epoch times are also plotted. Existing files for the same metrics are replaced. Training and validation aggregators receive default blue and orange styles when explicit styles are not provided.

Parameters:

  • aggregator_list (list[MetricsAggregator]) – Metric aggregators whose epoch histories are plotted together.

  • color_styles_list (list[tuple[str, str]] | None) – Optional color and line-style pair for each aggregator.

  • plot_dir (str | Path | None) – Directory in which plots and CSV files are saved. If None, the global figures directory is used.

  • figsize (tuple) – Width and height of generated figures in inches.

Raises:

ValueError – If no aggregators are provided, aggregators contain different numbers of epochs or history entries, or no epochs have been recorded.

record(loss_dict: dict[str, Tensor | int | float], lr: Tensor | int | float | None = None, kwargs: dict[str, Tensor | int | float] | None = None) → None

Accumulate metrics from one batch.

Tensor values are detached, converted to floating point, averaged when necessary, and accumulated as Python scalars.

Parameters:

  • loss_dict (dict[str, torch.Tensor | int | float]) – Batch loss values keyed by metric name.

  • lr (torch.Tensor | int | float | None) – Learning rate associated with the batch.

  • kwargs (dict[str, torch.Tensor | int | float] | None) – Additional scalar values, such as annealing coefficients, to aggregate with the batch metrics.

record_epoch(logs: dict[str, float], replace_index: int = None, time_elapsed: float = None)

Store aggregated metrics for an epoch.

Metrics are appended to the epoch history by default. When replace_index is provided, an existing epoch entry is replaced instead. Batch accumulators are reset after the epoch is recorded.

Parameters:

  • logs (dict[str, float]) – Distributed epoch metrics keyed by metric name.

  • replace_index (int | None) – Index of an existing epoch entry to replace. If None, a new epoch is appended.

  • time_elapsed (float | None) – Elapsed time for the epoch. If None, NaN is recorded.

Returns:

The recorded epoch metrics.

Return type:

dict[str, float]

Raises:

  • RuntimeError – If distributed metric aggregation has not been performed before recording the epoch.

  • ValueError – If replacement is requested for a metric that has not previously been recorded.

reset_batch_losses()

Reset accumulated batch-level metrics.

Loss, auxiliary-value, learning-rate, and batch-count accumulators are cleared after at least one epoch has been submitted.

Warns:

UserWarning – If batch metrics are reset before any epoch has been submitted.

class S2D4P.generic.aggregator.RunningCovariance(distributed: Distributed, sum_x: Tensor | None = None, sum_xxT: Tensor | None = None, count: Tensor | None = None)

Bases: object

Accumulate statistics required to compute a covariance matrix.

Maintains the running sum of observations, sum of outer products, and sample count. Statistics can be reduced across distributed processes before the final mean and unbiased sample covariance are calculated.

Parameters:

  • distributed (Distributed) – Distributed runtime used to reduce accumulated statistics across processes.

  • sum_x (torch.Tensor | None) – Running sum of observations.

  • sum_xxT (torch.Tensor | None) – Running sum of observation outer products.

  • count (torch.Tensor | None) – Number of observations accumulated.

count: Tensor | None = None
distributed: Distributed
distributed_reduce()

Sum accumulated covariance statistics across distributed processes.

The running observation sum, outer-product sum, and sample count are reduced in place across all processes.

finalize(print_checks=False)

Compute the mean and unbiased sample covariance.

The covariance matrix is explicitly symmetrized before being returned. Optional diagnostic output reports symmetry error, minimum eigenvalue, sample count, and feature dimension.

Parameters:

print_checks (bool) – Whether to print numerical diagnostics for the calculated covariance matrix.

Returns:

Mean vector and covariance matrix moved to CPU.

Return type:

tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]

Raises:

ValueError – If fewer than two observations have been accumulated.

S2D4P.generic.distributed module

class S2D4P.generic.distributed.Distributed

Bases: object

Manage distributed execution state and collective communication.

The class initializes distributed training from standard rank environment variables when available. Otherwise, it configures single-process execution on CUDA when available or CPU as a fallback.

all_reduce_sum(local: Tensor)

Sum a tensor across all distributed processes.

The input tensor is modified in place with the globally reduced sum. Has no effect when distributed communication is not initialized.

Parameters:

local (torch.Tensor) – Local tensor to sum across processes.

barrier()

Synchronize all distributed processes.

Has no effect during single-process execution.

broadcast(local: Tensor, src=0)

Broadcast a tensor from one process to all distributed processes.

The input tensor is modified in place with the value from the source process. Has no effect when distributed communication is not initialized.

Parameters:

  • local (torch.Tensor) – Tensor containing the value to broadcast or receive.

  • src (int) – Rank of the source process.

cleanup()

Clean up distributed communication resources.

Destroys the active process group when distributed communication has been initialized.

S2D4P.generic.logger module

S2D4P.generic.logger.setup_logger(name: str = 'trainer', log_dir: str | Path | None = None, rank: int = 0, level: int = 20) → Logger

Configure and return an application logger.

The root process writes log messages to standard output and to a log file. Non-root processes receive the configured logger without adding output handlers. Existing handlers are reused to avoid duplicate log messages.

Parameters:

  • name (str) – Name assigned to the logger and its output log file.

  • log_dir (str | Path | None) – Directory in which the log file is created. If None, the directory is obtained from the GLOBAL_LOG_DIR environment variable.

  • rank (int) – Process rank. Console and file handlers are configured only for rank zero.

  • level (int) – Logging level applied to the logger and its handlers.

Returns:

Configured logger instance.

Return type:

logging.Logger

S2D4P.generic.monitoring module

class S2D4P.generic.monitoring.Monitor(*, cpu: bool = True, ram: bool = True, gpu0: bool = False, gpu1: bool = False, gpus: Iterable[int] | None = None, interval: float = 0.1, rank: int = 0, local_rank: int = 0, world_size: int = 1)

Bases: object

Monitor process resource utilization and execution stages.

Resource samples are collected periodically in a background thread and can include process CPU usage, resident memory, and utilization and memory usage for selected GPUs. Named spans and checkpoints can be recorded alongside resource samples to associate utilization with execution stages.

Parameters:

  • cpu (bool) – Whether to collect process CPU utilization.

  • ram (bool) – Whether to collect process resident memory usage.

  • gpu0 (bool) – Whether to monitor physical GPU index 0.

  • gpu1 (bool) – Whether to monitor physical GPU index 1.

  • gpus (Iterable[int] | None) – Additional physical GPU indices to monitor.

  • interval (float) – Sampling interval in seconds.

  • rank (int) – Global rank associated with the monitored process.

  • local_rank (int) – Local rank associated with the monitored process.

  • world_size (int) – Number of processes participating in the distributed execution.

checkpoint(name: str) → None

Record an instantaneous named checkpoint.

The checkpoint name is qualified by the currently active monitoring stage when applicable.

Parameters:

name (str) – Name of the checkpoint.

Raises:

  • TypeError – If name is not a string.

  • ValueError – If name is empty after removing surrounding whitespace.

plot(df: Any = None, metrics: Iterable[str] | None = None, save_path: str | PathLike[str] | None = None, show: bool = True, smooth: str | None = None, **smooth_kwargs: Any)

Plot resource utilization together with the execution timeline.

Resource samples are displayed in separate metric panels while completed spans and checkpoints are shown on a timeline. Metrics may optionally be smoothed before display.

Parameters:

  • df (Any) – Monitoring dataframe to plot. If None, recorded monitoring events are used.

  • metrics (Iterable[str] | None) – Resource metrics to plot. If None, all collected metrics containing valid data are selected.

  • save_path (str | os.PathLike[str] | None) – Path at which to save the generated figure.

  • show (bool) – Whether to display the figure interactively.

  • smooth (str | None) – Optional smoothing method applied to plotted metric values.

  • **smooth_kwargs (Any) – Additional arguments passed to the selected smoothing method.

Returns:

Generated Matplotlib figure, or None if there are no events or no usable resource samples to plot.

Return type:

Any

Raises:

  • TypeError – If metrics is provided as a single string instead of an iterable of metric names.

  • ValueError – If required dataframe columns are missing or a requested metric was not collected.

S2D4P.generic.monitoring.build_distributed_monitor(distributed: Distributed, *, cpu: bool = True, ram: bool = True, gpu: bool = True, interval: float = 0.1) → Monitor

Build a resource monitor for a distributed process.

When GPU monitoring is enabled, the process’s local CUDA rank is resolved to a physical GPU index for NVML monitoring. Failure to resolve the GPU does not disable CPU or RAM monitoring.

Parameters:

  • distributed (Distributed) – Distributed runtime containing rank, local-rank, and world-size information.

  • cpu (bool) – Whether to collect process CPU utilization.

  • ram (bool) – Whether to collect process resident memory usage.

  • gpu (bool) – Whether to monitor the GPU assigned to the distributed process.

  • interval (float) – Sampling interval in seconds.

Returns:

Resource monitor configured for the distributed process.

Return type:

Monitor

S2D4P.generic.monitoring.combine_rank_results(output_dir: str | PathLike[str], world_size: int) → Path | None

Combine resource-monitoring CSV files from multiple ranks.

Available rank files are concatenated and, when possible, sorted by timestamp and rank before being written to a combined CSV file.

Parameters:

  • output_dir (str | os.PathLike[str]) – Directory containing per-rank monitoring CSV files.

  • world_size (int) – Number of distributed ranks expected to have produced monitoring files.

Returns:

Path to the combined CSV file, or None if no rank files are found.

Return type:

Path | None

Raises:

  • TypeError – If world_size is not an integer.

  • ValueError – If world_size is not positive.

S2D4P.generic.monitoring.distributed_monitoring(distributed: Distributed, output_dir: str | os.PathLike[str], *, cpu: bool = True, ram: bool = True, gpu: bool = True, interval: float = 0.1, combine_ranks: bool = True) → Iterator

Monitor resources within a distributed execution context.

Monitoring starts when the context is entered and records whether execution completed or was interrupted. Results are exported when leaving the context. After successful completion, ranks synchronize and the root process can combine per-rank monitoring results.

Parameters:

  • distributed (Distributed) – Distributed runtime associated with the monitored process.

  • output_dir (str | os.PathLike[str]) – Directory in which monitoring results are written.

  • cpu (bool) – Whether to collect process CPU utilization.

  • ram (bool) – Whether to collect process resident memory usage.

  • gpu (bool) – Whether to monitor the GPU assigned to each distributed process.

  • interval (float) – Sampling interval in seconds.

  • combine_ranks (bool) – Whether the root process combines per-rank CSV files after successful completion.

Yields:

Monitor – Active resource monitor for the current distributed process.

tuple[Path | None, Path | None]

S2D4P.generic.monitoring.resolve_physical_gpu_index(local_rank: int) → int

Resolve a local CUDA rank to its physical GPU index.

When CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is unset, the local rank is treated as the physical GPU index. Numeric visible-device entries are resolved directly, while GPU UUIDs are matched against physical devices through NVML.

Parameters:

local_rank (int) – Zero-based local CUDA rank to resolve.

Returns:

Physical GPU index corresponding to local_rank.

Return type:

int

Raises:

  • TypeError – If local_rank is not an integer.

  • ValueError – If local_rank is negative or outside the visible-device range, a visible-device identifier is unsupported, or a GPU UUID cannot be resolved through NVML.

class S2D4P.generic.runtime.RuntimeContext(GLOBAL_EXP_DIR: Path | str | None = <factory>, GLOBAL_CHECKPOINT_DIR: Path | str | None = None, GLOBAL_FIGURES_DIR: Path | str | None = None, GLOBAL_LOG_DIR: Path | str | None = None, GLOBAL_MONITORING_DIR: Path | str | None = None, GLOBAL_OUTPUT_DIR: Path | str | None = None, INPUT_VAR_METADATA: dict | None = None, TARGET_VAR_METADATA: dict | None = None)

Bases: object

Store global runtime paths and variable metadata.

Provides shared experiment directories and input and target metadata used across training, inference, logging, checkpointing, monitoring, and output workflows.

Parameters:

  • GLOBAL_EXP_DIR (Path | str | None) – Root directory for the current experiment.

  • GLOBAL_CHECKPOINT_DIR (Path | str | None) – Directory used to store model checkpoints. If None, defaults to the checkpoints directory under GLOBAL_EXP_DIR.

  • GLOBAL_FIGURES_DIR (Path | str | None) – Directory used to store generated figures. If None, defaults to the figures directory under GLOBAL_EXP_DIR.

  • GLOBAL_LOG_DIR (Path | str | None) – Directory used to store log files. If None, defaults to the logs directory under GLOBAL_EXP_DIR.

  • GLOBAL_MONITORING_DIR (Path | str | None) – Directory used to store resource-monitoring outputs. If None, defaults to the resource_monitoring directory under GLOBAL_EXP_DIR.

  • GLOBAL_OUTPUT_DIR (Path | str | None) – Directory used to store inference outputs. If None, defaults to the inference directory under GLOBAL_EXP_DIR.

  • INPUT_VAR_METADATA (dict | None) – Metadata describing model input variables and preprocessing.

  • TARGET_VAR_METADATA (dict | None) – Metadata describing model target variables and preprocessing.
